headline: Bitcoin dropped to about $62,100 in Asian trading on Sunday, its weakest level since mid-July, as roughly $2 billion of leveraged crypto bets were force-closed and money kept flowing out of crypto funds.

market.asOf: CoinMarketCap coin pages read at about 03:59 UTC Sun 15 Nov (10:59 Bangkok). CoinGecko could not be opened this run, and CoinMarketCap's homepage table showed a different snapshot (BTC $65,916). Prices have moved since; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear by both readings: CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index showed 15 to 16 out of 100 at about 03:59 UTC Sunday, and TokenPost reported the Crypto Fear & Greed Index at 10, in its extreme fear range.

stories.title: Bitcoin and ether hit their lowest since July as about $2B of borrowed bets are wiped out
stories.summary: The sell-off spread into Sunday in Asia. Bitcoin fell to about $62,100 and ether to about $1,711. Traders who had borrowed to bet on rising prices were forced out of their positions automatically, and that forced selling pushed prices lower still.
points: Bitcoin fell as low as $62,112 in Asia on Sunday, its weakest since July 14, per Bloomberg via Business Standard.
Bitcoin is down about 25% since 21 October; its 2026 low is $57,742, set on 1 July, per Bloomberg.
Ether fell another 3.4% on Sunday to $1,711, its lowest since July 8, per Bloomberg.
About $2B of crypto bets were liquidated (force-closed) in the 24 hours to 9am Sunday Singapore time, including $774M in bitcoin and $488M in ether, per Coinglass data cited by Bloomberg.
Bitcoin broke below its 200-day moving average, a widely watched long-term trend line, of about $73,000, said Rich Rosenblum of GSR, per Bloomberg.

sources.label: Bloomberg via Business Standard: four-month low

stories.title: Money keeps leaving crypto: ETF withdrawals, shrinking stablecoins, and XRP at a two-year low
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, the way many Americans hold bitcoin in a brokerage account, lost more than $1B for a second week. The supply of stablecoins, the digital dollars traders keep ready to buy coins, is shrinking fast. Both mean fewer buyers in the market.
points: Spot bitcoin ETFs had $1.07B of net outflows last week and have seen outflows for seven straight trading days, per The Block.
Spot ether ETFs lost $398.9M, their seventh straight losing week, per The Block.
Stablecoin supply fell $17B over the last month, the steepest drop since 2022, per Glassnode data cited by CoinDesk.
XRP fell to $0.89, its lowest since November 2024, and US XRP ETFs had $19.13M of net outflows last week, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: A near-certain December rate hike and a giant AI stock listing hang over the week
stories.summary: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive and tend to pull money away from riskier assets such as crypto. Futures markets expect the Fed to raise rates on 9 December. Some analysts also say Anthropic's huge stock listing this week may be drawing money away from crypto. These are market bets and opinions, not decisions.
points: CME FedWatch showed 88.5% odds of a quarter-point hike in December and 11.5% for a half-point hike, per Bitcoin.com News, up from 76.3% for a hike on 6 November.
October consumer prices rose 0.4% against a 0.3% forecast, and payrolls rose 165,000 against about 65,000 expected, per Bitcoin.com News.
Anthropic and some existing shareholders plan to sell up to $64.4B of shares at $70 to $78 each, with Nasdaq trading under ANT due on 19 November, per The Next Web.
Price action "looks very similar to what happened through the SpaceX IPO pricing period," said Richard Galvin of DACM, per Bloomberg.

briefs.title: US moves to seize over $1.2B from the Binance hack
briefs.summary: The Justice Department said a court authorized seizing more than $1.2B stolen in the Binance hack, which it tied to North Korea, and that efforts have frozen more than $2.7B.

briefs.title: Trump names new SEC and CFTC commissioners
briefs.summary: Trump nominated Democrats Kristin Johnson (SEC) and Matthew Rowland (CFTC), alongside Republicans Steven Levine (SEC) and Nathan Anonick (CFTC), per Banking Dive.

briefs.title: Ethereum Foundation sells 7,500 ETH
briefs.summary: The Ethereum Foundation sold 7,500 ETH over four days for roughly $14.5M as ether fell, per Shattered.

briefs.title: Russia opens crypto buying to retail investors
briefs.summary: Regulated Russian intermediaries can sell bitcoin, ether and USDT to retail investors from 17 November, capped at 300,000 rubles a year per intermediary, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Bitcoin trades into a modeled liquidation zone
briefs.summary: Glassnode's 11 November analysis placed the largest modeled cluster of forced-selling levels between $59,500 and $62,600, per Cryptonews.

briefs.title: Kava Lend hacked for about $3.8M
briefs.summary: An attacker drained about 55.2M KAVA through a dormant BUSD market, and the KAVA token fell nearly 40%, per The Block.
